claims.statement: The public API of sincpro-framework is exactly what sincpro_framework/__init__.py re-exports (ApplicationService, DataTransferObject, Feature, UseFramework, logger, Middleware, TypeDTO, TypeDTOResponse) from a single Poetry package that downstream SDKs such as sincpro_payments_sdk import, so those exported names and their signatures are a compatibility surface while internal modules such as ioc.py are not re-exported and stay free to change.

The distribution ships an empty py.typed marker plus five hand-written stubs (use_bus.pyi, bus.pyi, sincpro_abstractions.pyi, aio/bus.pyi, context/framework_context.pyi) that mirror their modules, so the stub is what type checkers read and any signature change must be mirrored there in the same change or every consumer's checker keeps reading the old contract.

A new public surface needs its own stub entry as well as its runtime implementation: Bus.thread_context() and Bus.get_async_bus() are declared in sincpro_abstractions.pyi while their implementations live in context/thread_context_bus.py and aio/bus.py, and aio/bus.pyi mirrors AsyncBus with async execute/__call__ overloads.

The return_type argument is a static-typing device only: UseFramework.__call__ forwards it to the middleware pipeline as a keyword, its local executor calls self.bus.execute(processed_dto) without it, and all three Bus.execute implementations accept and ignore the parameter, so IDE return-type narrowing comes from the stub overloads rather than from runtime behaviour.

Each UseFramework instance owns its own FrameworkContainer built in __init__ with the two registration decorators bound to it as functools.partial objects, and the container declares feature_bus and app_service_bus as Singletons, so two bounded contexts in one process never share a registry or a bus.

Every registration stores its own providers.Factory entry (per DTO name, in both layers) and a handler instance is produced only when the build evaluates those providers via the container's framework_bus() Factory, so registration itself never instantiates a Feature or ApplicationService.

The routing key of the whole framework is the input DTO class __name__: registration writes the registries under dto.__name__ and every execution path looks the handler up by dto.__class__.__name__, so changing to class objects or qualified names would invalidate every existing registry key.

FrameworkBus enforces single-layer registration: its constructor intersects the two registry key sets and raises DTOAlreadyRegistered with the colliding names, execute re-checks the same collision on every call, and a name in neither registry raises UnknownDTOToExecute.

Observability may never change what the bus does and is never required: the package documents that every method is a no-op with neither extra installed, _shielded catches failures on enter and exit but re-raises the block's own exception and ignores a suppressing __exit__ on purpose, and record_error wraps its whole body in a swallowing try/except.

All three buses of one framework share the single Observability object, which is what makes ignore_sentry_exceptions applied after the build reach both sub-buses without any propagation call, and build_root_bus re-assigns it defensively so the guarantee does not depend on the container provider the facade captured.

The identity of the emitting library is captured by caller_module() during Observability construction and the ObservabilityIdentity is resolved lazily once on first use, because resolving the caller later would name the host application (Odoo) instead of the SDK that built the bus; a second build_root_bus() reuses the same Observability and identity.

Handlers get access to the live context only because build_root_bus calls _bind_context_to_handlers(), which invokes bind_to_framework(self) on every value of both registries, after which ContextConsumer.context resolves through that binder rather than through its empty fallback dict.

The middleware pipeline protects the routing key: after running the chain it re-assigns processed_dto.__class__ to the original DTO class whenever a middleware returned a different type, which is what lets a middleware enrich a DTO without turning the call into UnknownDTOToExecute.

bus.dto_registry is the description contract of the bus, snapshotted from the container at build time, and introspection skips any registry key it cannot find there — so handlers wired through register_feature/register_app_service are callable but invisible to features()/app_services()/dtos() and therefore to every entrypoint host.

build_root_bus sets was_initialized = True before materialising the facade, so a build that raises leaves the instance flagged as initialized with bus still None and every later framework(dto) raises SincproFrameworkNotBuilt instead of retrying the build.

Both registries are keyed by the input DTO class __name__ and each name carries its own providers.Factory, so a class registered for several DTOs (the list form) is instantiated once per name and the names do not share a handler object; no test in the repository asserts handler identity or count, so this is a deduction from dependency-injector's Factory semantics rather than a pinned behaviour.

The repository has settled homes for new capabilities: entrypoints/ takes a new wire but must reuse Catalog and keep protocol types out of catalog.py, aio/ takes async-only additions, context/ takes per-thread context hand-off, introspection/ stays the single reader of the registries, and observability/ owns tracing and error reporting so bus.py and use_bus.py never import opentelemetry or sentry_sdk.

A new async or thread-crossing handle follows a three-place pattern — a concrete method on the Bus ABC, an implementation module that keeps its back-reference to Bus behind if TYPE_CHECKING with quoted forward references to break the circular import, and a stub entry — and the pyright ignore comments next to self._bus.execute exist because Bus is only resolvable under TYPE_CHECKING, making an import-shape change there a typing risk.

A new protocol host must declare its library as an optional extra and import it lazily inside the method that needs it, raising a named ImportError that tells the user which extra to install, because the local dev group installs the optional SDKs unconditionally and would not catch a module-scope import that makes an extra mandatory.

The source flags a caveat rather than a contract in the registration plumbing: the duplicate check reads feature_bus.kwargs / app_service_bus.kwargs while entries are attached with add_attributes(...) and read back from .attributes at build time, and how add_attributes surfaces on .kwargs is dependency-injector behaviour that no test in the repository exercises.

The list form of the registration decorator is deliberately non-atomic: _register_service loops over the normalised DTO list and mutates the layer registry and dto_registry per element, so a collision on a later element leaves the earlier names already registered and the container partially updated when DTOAlreadyRegistered escapes.

The internal DTORegistration alias admits a bare str, but _register_service reads __name__ off every element unconditionally and nothing resolves a string to a class, so a str element would fail on attribute access; the public stub narrows the decorator argument to classes and lists of classes and is the accurate contract.

Free-threading is explicitly not implemented or targeted, and three concrete gaps are recorded in the source as current-implementation notes rather than guarantees: importing dependency-injector silently re-enables the GIL for the whole process on python3.14t, _live_overlays is a plain unlocked list whose only iteration copies it first, and dynamic_dep_registry is a lock-free dict whose add_dependency docstring says to call it during startup and not concurrently with in-flight requests.

FeatureBus and ApplicationServiceBus are constructible without the container and without an Observability argument, fall back to a default Observability, and their register_feature/register_app_service methods are documented as not the intended path — the decorator is — because they bypass dto_registry.

The container declares an injected_dependencies provider that no code in the package ever reads; the live dependency path is dynamic_dep_registry pushed onto the registration entries at build time plus the read-only DependencyLocator behind framework.deps.

Because the decorated classes are registered into the container that the decorator partial captured, a service module must be imported after the instance it registers against exists, and a module that is never imported contributes nothing — the situation SincproFrameworkNotBuilt's message points at.

The typing gate of this repository is make lint (pyright over sincpro_framework and tests), not the typing_cases test, because that test skips when neither a pyright nor a poetry executable is available; a new typing feature is exercised by adding a case under tests/typing_and_linter/typing_cases, where the typed-deps, typed-context and list-registration examples live.

The OpenWiki agent reads .openwikiignore rather than .gitignore and the file states that explicitly, so any capability whose only documentation would be an ignored path (secrets, dist/, poetry.lock, coverage artifacts, caches) cannot be documented from that path.

The stubs are part of the package's declared type contract rather than tooling output: the distribution ships py.typed in the same package directory as the .pyi files, and the .pyi files carry the docstrings and overloads that IDE users rely on, so a stub that drifts from its module is a shipped defect rather than a lint warning.
